match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the Units 3 and 4 idea of internal versus external validity: psy-judging-research treats validity broadly as measuring the claimed thing and is aimed at Units 1 and 2, and the biology card covers fair-test validity without the idea that results must apply beyond the sample.

draft.title: Validity
card: Whether a study measured what it set out to measure. It is weakened when other variables, such as extraneous or confounding variables, may have affected the results.
Whether the results apply beyond the sample, to other people, places and times. A sample that is small or unlike the wider population weakens it.
A study can be strong on one kind of validity and weak on the other. A tightly controlled lab study may have high internal validity but results that do not carry over to everyday life.
To judge validity, ask two questions. Did the study test what it claimed to? Would the findings hold for people outside the sample?
draft.remember: Internal: did it measure the right thing? External: do the results apply beyond the sample?

a.q: A study tests a new memory strategy. Students using it also get an extra hour of study time, so the results may not be due to the strategy. Which kind of validity is weakened?
opts: Internal, as another variable may explain the results
External, as the sample may be too small
Internal, as the sample is too small
External, as another variable may explain the results
a.why: The extra study time is another variable that may explain the results, so the study may not have measured the effect of the strategy alone. That is a problem of internal validity. Sample size and wider application concern external validity.
a.clue: Did the study isolate the strategy it set out to test?

b.q: Dr Rao tests a sleep program with 20 university students in Melbourne. Results are measured well and other variables are controlled. She then claims it works for all Australians. What is the best judgement?
opts: Internal validity may be high, but external is limited
External validity is high, as the study was well controlled
Both are low, as the sample was small
Internal validity is low, as the sample was only students
b.why: Good control of other variables supports internal validity. The sample is 20 university students, so claiming the result applies to all Australians goes beyond what it supports, which limits external validity. Control of variables does not make results apply more widely.
b.clue: Separate the quality of the measuring from who was in the sample.
